lead: the house has stood twenty-two years — the loft, the child through school, a mortgage nearly finished. what the neighbourhood knows about who lives in it is one sentence, said once, to one person, and passed on by them since.
sun: nothing about the place is disguised or temporary. you put it up in the ordinary way — the roof done properly, the boiler replaced before it went, the will drawn so the child lands well whichever of you goes first — and people come in, eat, stay over, and take the arrangement as the shape of the street. a room that carries its load stops being a subject.
moon: one item in it is under cover, and the covering is a form of words from the first year: friends, sharing the place, sensible about money. everyone repeats it because you have never had to say it again. nothing else props it. one direct question at the wrong table, from somebody entitled to ask, and the whole account comes off in a single piece, with the house standing untouched underneath.
pull: what you built will outlast the two of you and needs nothing from anybody. what stands over it is one sentence from the first year, and nothing else is holding that up.
tension: the child is grown and asks nothing, which is its own weather. what arrives instead is other people's certainty: an aunt who has decided one thing, a colleague who has decided another, both fond, both wrong, both acting on it — the seating at a funeral, who gets told first when somebody is ill. correcting any of it means saying the whole thing in a room that has spent twenty-two years not having heard it.
cost: a home that has carried a child's whole schooling and two redundancies came out of an arrangement most people could not have made hold for a year, and it has never once wobbled. the covering over it was never built, only said, and it has needed no maintenance because nobody has tested it. it holds until somebody asks.

lead: nothing you have built has come down, and nobody has ever raised any of it, and there is no part of you set against either — no showy half, no ledger, no second version that would say so.
sun: a new person arrives at the firm, or marries into the family, and what you set up years before is already the way things are done — met as the standing conditions, never as anybody's decision. nothing you have made carries a moment of being introduced. it was not there, and then it was, and the changeover produced no event, which is why nobody in the building can name the year it started.
moon: no moment is generated at which you would check. the holding does not register as effort while it is happening, so it never comes up for review — not the total, not whether it was worth it, not whether anybody was going to say. taking a reading on your own load would need an occasion, and a structure that has never faltered supplies none.
pull: everything holding your life up was put there by you, and no conversation about any of it has ever needed to happen. doubled, there is nothing anywhere for anybody to point at, including you.
tension: kindness has no way in. people who love you go looking for the thing to do — the visit that helps, the job taken off you, the favour returned — and find a life with no rough edge to take hold of, so they do the next thing available, which is to assume you are fine and ring less. the arrangement never has a bad week, so the offer never has anywhere to go.
cost: twenty years on, something you set up in a bad year is still running without a meeting, a review, or one hour of anybody's doubt about whether it will be there — which almost nothing in an ordinary life manages. no account of you exists out there, and none exists in here either. the one event that would produce either is a collapse, and nothing here collapses.

lead: you have gone as far as the car park with eleven of them, and no further. each walks in alone, and four streets away the place they trained in is doing exactly what it did before any of them arrived.
sun: the practice is the thing you actually made: the rooms, the rota, the way a difficult morning gets handled, all of it set up years ago and running now without correction. nobody inside it is being taken anywhere. they arrive into a working set of conditions, do a decade, and leave, and at no point does the place require anyone to think about who arranged it that way.
moon: the walking out is one at a time and it stops early by design. you take a person the last stretch of something they could not route themselves through — the referral, the interview at the bigger place — and you halt at the boundary, because the going was yours and the arriving is theirs. what happens on the other side has never been your business.
pull: eleven people can name the morning you walked them somewhere. the place that made all eleven gets named by nobody, and the walk was the smaller of the two things by a distance.
tension: two of them have said it years later, half-joking — that you dropped them the day they got in. it describes the conduct accurately and misses what it was. the handing over is where the work ends, and no part of you follows a person into their own life. so the coolness they felt at the exact moment they were most grateful is the one thing you have never found a way to answer.
cost: nothing is owed to you afterwards. no hook is left in, nobody keeps reporting, and a handover that clean is rarer than it sounds. gratitude goes to the escort. the years of arranging that put eleven people within reach of those doors contain no moment where anybody was accompanied anywhere, and no version of the car park exists for the part that took the decades.

lead: thirty-one years of letters with someone you have been in a room with four times. everything else in your keeping is built and standing and asks nothing; that one length has needed pulling every month since you were twenty-three.
sun: what you make is designed to hold without attention, and it does — the household, the two committees, the arrangement your brother's family has lived inside since his firm went. all of it is up, all of it carries, and none of it requires a weekly act from you. that is the entire technique, and it has produced a life in which almost nothing has to be maintained by hand.
moon: the correspondence is the exception and it is not built at all. it is held, at both ends, by two people continuing to pull — no shared house, no committee, no standing arrangement carrying it between letters. a slack year would not damage it. a slack year would end it, without anybody deciding anything, and there is no material in it that would hold a shape on its own.
pull: you have never had to maintain anything you built. the one thing you could not survive losing has no structure in it, and exists only while both of you are pulling.
tension: the obvious move is to make it permanent — a fixed week every year, a place you both own a share of, something that would go on existing during a bad stretch. every version of that has been drafted in your head and none has been proposed, because a structure would take the pulling out, and the pulling is what the thing consists of. people near you call it a funny sort of friendship.
cost: holding one line at full tension for three decades, with no house, no committee and no shared property under it, is a thing most people cannot manage for eighteen months. everything else you own would survive a year of your absence intact. the exception cannot be propped, delegated or left standing, and it needs the other end alive on the same day as yours.
